First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{6}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{10} + \sqrt{6},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{6}} & = \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{6}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6}} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6})}{(\sqrt{10})^{2}-(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6})}{10-6} & = \\ \frac{6(\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6})}{4} & = \\ \frac{3(\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{6})}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
